S3_amortisation_audit.question: is every cost counted at every N, or is something frozen while the logic grows?
terms_to_track_per_N: E_gate_drive_idealPWL (the 'floor' row's driver term) -- SIGN CHECK
E_timer (0 or 3.5227 fJ) -- fixed per bank, so per-gate falls as 1/N
E_wellrail (vhi) -- computed by the instrument but NOT in the ledger sum
E_ideal_inputs_bank1 -- ideal DC sources, not in the ledger
buck / converter resupply of E_tank_loss -- NOT SIMULATED AT ALL

S3a_negative_driver_credit.hypothesis_PRE_STATED: the floor row's driver term is NEGATIVE and grows more negative with N, so the 'floor' is a CREDIT, not a floor
S3a_negative_driver_credit.test: measure E_gate_drive_idealPWL_per_bank at every N I run; if < 0, recompute the floor row with the driver floored at its PHYSICAL minimum of ZERO (a perfectly recovering driver nets zero, never negative)
S3a_negative_driver_credit.pre_stated_consequence: N=64 goes from 4.1034 (0.991x) to E_tank/64 ~ 4.174 (1.008x) and the crossing at N=64 DISAPPEARS; first crossing moves to N=128
S3a_negative_driver_credit.if_wrong: report that the subsidy is negligible and the crossing stands

S3b_real_driver_convention.hypothesis_PRE_STATED: Q_abs = |Q_close| + |Q_open| double-counts a conventional driver. A conventional driver pays Q_close*V on the RISE of the gate and NOTHING from the supply on the FALL (the stored half is dumped to ground). So E_real_per_gate_cycle = |Q_close|*V, and per QAL cycle (two gate cycles) = (|Q_close_rise| + |Q_close_return|)*V.
S3b_real_driver_convention.test: extract Q_close and Q_open SEPARATELY per device from my own rows and check |Q_open|/|Q_close|
S3b_real_driver_convention.pre_stated_consequence: if |Q_open| ~ |Q_close| then Phase 2 amendment A1's per-CYCLE figure is ~2x the real driver cost, and Phase 1's rise-hop figure was already the correct FULL-CYCLE number
S3b_real_driver_convention.pre_stated_numbers: N=64 buildable row ~11.5 fJ/gate (2.78x), NOT 18.756 (4.53x); conclusion 'no crossing on the buildable row' STANDS either way

S3c_buck.test: compute the converter efficiency eta at which the floor row stops crossing, since E_tank_loss is exactly what a converter must resupply and no converter is simulated
S3c_buck.pre_stated: eta_breakeven ~ 0.88 at N=256 and ~0.93 at N=128; below that there is no crossing at any N

S3d_wellrail_double_count.hypothesis_PRE_STATED: E_wellrail is NEGATIVE (the 1.5 V well supply RECEIVES charge). The charge it receives came through the switch from the tank, so it is ALREADY inside the MEASURED tank droop. Adding |E_wellrail| as an extra cost DOUBLE-COUNTS and is the wrong SIGN of correction.
S3d_wellrail_double_count.test: per-bank sign and magnitude of E_wellrail; A6 tank-closure residual (does the tank droop equal net energy out of the tank?); and, if time allows, a control row with the switch pMOS bulk moved OFF vhi
S3d_wellrail_double_count.note: this correction goes AGAINST my own other findings and will be reported as such

S4_scale_invariance_independent.instrument: up.py's own cellchain (5 inverters, fixed DC rail, stage 3 measured)
S4_scale_invariance_independent.rerun: variants A (real chain, CLOAD 2 fF fixed), B (pure coscale), C (FIXED LOAD = the positive control), D (QAL-bias unpowered load), at s = 1/2/4/8, rail 1.65 V
S4_scale_invariance_independent.PASS: reproduce each ratio within 2%, and C must be much steeper than A (that is what proves A's flatness is a measurement and not a dead probe)

S4_NEW_CONTROL_variant_E.why: the record's own caveat is that qal/sg13lv_compat.sp DISCARDS ad/as/pd/ps, so junction capacitance is W-INDEPENDENT in every deck in this campaign. A fixed self-load is exactly what 1/s dilution feeds on, so variant A's 28% improvement is an UPPER bound and real silicon would be FLATTER.
S4_NEW_CONTROL_variant_E.test: variant A plus an EXPLICIT lumped capacitor of (s-1)*C_j per cell output node, emulating AD proportional to W, with C_j taken from my OWN variant-difference solve
S4_NEW_CONTROL_variant_E.pre_stated: if the caveat is right, variant E is FLATTER than A -- ratio closer to 1 -- and the scale-invariance finding is STRONGER than the record's numbers show
S4_NEW_CONTROL_variant_E.falsification: if E is STEEPER than A the caveat is backwards and I must say so

S6_verdict_rule.question: does QAL deliver HIGHER PERFORMANCE at an area/power cost, and at what N and scale?
S6_verdict_rule.performance_unit: ONE LEVEL. Both technologies evaluate a level's gates in parallel, so gates/ps is NOT a throughput win. CMOS bar 92.8 ps/level.
S6_verdict_rule.decision: if level time is >= CMOS at every (N, s) then the answer is NO on the performance axis regardless of what the energy does, and I will say so without hedging
S6_verdict_rule.energy_bar: 4.14 fJ/cell/op is the hard bar; 10.0831 fJ/inverter-cycle is the easy one and means nothing
